We have the runtime shared libraries (`libc.so.6`, `libm.so.6`, etc.) but not the development symlinks (`libc.so`, `libm.so`) nor linker scripts. We can create symlinks in a local directory and point the linker to it via `-L`. But we don't have root; however we can create symlinks in a user-writable dir. The issue is `libc.so` normally is a linker script that references libc.so.6 and libc_nonshared.a. We might be able to just symlink `libc.so -> libc.so.6`. Linking directly against the shared library may work for simple programs, though some symbols (like `__libc_start_main`) need libc_nonshared.a? Actually for dynamic linking with glibc, `-lc` typically finds `libc.so` which is a linker script including libc_nonshared.a for static parts. But symlinking to .so.6 often works for simple programs.

Also `libgcc_s.so.1` exists but no `libgcc_s.so`. Let me create a shim dir in /tmp or project with symlinks, then use `-L` via RUSTFLAGS.

Let me try. Create /tmp/opencode/libshim with symlinks: libc.so -> /lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6, libm.so -> libm.so.6, libgcc_s.so -> libgcc_s.so.1, libpthread.so -> libpthread.so.0, libdl.so -> libdl.so.2, librt.so -> librt.so.1, libutil.so -> libutil.so.1.

Then rustc -L /tmp/opencode/libshim -C linker=rust-lld. But rust-lld with `-Bdynamic` will search for -lc. Order of -L should include shim.

parts.text:
The link succeeded but `_start` missing → segfault. The issue: glibc's `Scrt1.o` / `crt1.o` start files aren't being used. Normally gcc passes crt1.o. Rust with a C linker relies on the linker finding Scrt1.o via the compiler driver. With rust-lld invoked directly, we need to provide the crt objects and dynamic linker.

We need `Scrt1.o`, `crti.o`, `crtn.o` from libc-dev. They're not present. Hmm. Let me check if they exist somewhere.

This is getting into the weeds. The environment lacks a C toolchain / libc dev. Building a Rust binary here may be infeasible without more work. 

Alternative: We can write our own `_start`? That's very hacky. Actually, we could use `-C link-self-contained`? Rust's `rust-lld` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` target uses self-contained. But glibc target doesn't. We could add the musl target via rustup — musl target ships self-contained CRT objects and musl libc, and rust-lld can link it fully self-contained! That's the clean solution: `rustup target add aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`. Then build with `--target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`. Rust ships self-contained musl components (crt, libc) for musl targets? Let me check. Historically rustup's musl target includes self-contained musl libc and crt. Yes, `rust-lld` + musl self-contained works.
